item.title: AI Factories
item.description: An AI factory gives startups, companies, the public sector and researchers access to GPU capacity and AI services. In Waldur that access is a catalog: inference endpoints with API keys, virtual machines with GPUs on OpenNebula or OpenStack, and Kubernetes namespaces with GPU quotas, ordered by organizations that have been onboarded, and either paid for or counted against an allocation.

item.title: Cloud and GPU Providers
item.description: Data center operators, regional and sovereign clouds, and GPU clouds sell compute to many customers. Waldur is the part their customers deal with: a catalog with price plans, ordering, organizations and projects, metering and monthly invoices. Underneath, the provider keeps the platforms it already runs, such as OpenStack, VMware, OpenNebula, Kubernetes or Slurm.

item.title: Digital Marketplace
item.description: A digital marketplace lets public bodies buy IT services from vetted providers through one catalog, with ordering, provisioning and invoicing done online instead of a separate procurement for every purchase. In Waldur, providers publish offerings with their price plans, the operator decides who may publish and what goes on sale, and public bodies order within the rules the operator sets.

item.title: Government Cloud
item.description: A government cloud is run by a central IT authority for ministries and agencies. Waldur is the self-service layer of such a cloud: agencies order resources from a catalog, every resource belongs to an agency and a project, and the authority sees usage and costs per agency.

item.title: HPC Center
item.description: HPC centers serve research groups, companies and national or European projects, each with an allocation of its own. Waldur gives them one portal for all of it: users request access or apply in a call, project leads manage their members, and the center sees usage per project. Slurm and MOAB clusters are connected through the Waldur Site Agent.

item.title: NREN
item.description: National research and education networks offer services to universities and research institutes, and often coordinate the services that their members provide to each other. Waldur gives an NREN one catalog for both: its own services, such as cloud, storage or collaboration tools, and the services that member institutions publish as providers. Users sign in with their institutional identity.

item.title: Peer Review Portal
item.description: Funding agencies, research infrastructures and computing centres often hand out resources through calls: researchers and companies apply, experts review the proposals, and a panel decides. Waldur runs that process from the call to the allocation, and turns each decision into a project with its resources on the providers’ systems.

item.title: Self-service for Internal IT
item.description: IT departments provide servers, storage, software and support to the rest of the company. Waldur gives them a catalog where departments order these services. Each request is either provisioned automatically or turned into a ticket in the service desk the IT team already uses, so its back-office processes stay as they are.
